chunks: And al-Sheikh — may Allah the Exalted support him — informed me; he said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn al-Walid informed me, from his father, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban — both together — from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Hammad, from Rib'i, from al-Fudayl, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him):
He said: «There is no objection to a man urinating in flowing water, and it is disliked to urinate in stagnant water.»

Then al-Sheikh — may Allah the Exalted support him — said: When a person enters a house in which a toilet has been built facing the qibla or with one's back to it, that does not harm him; the dislike applies only in open areas and places where it is possible to turn away from the qibla. Its explanation has already passed in what preceded.

Then he said: If on a person's left hand there is a ring on whose bezel is engraved a name from the names of Allah the Exalted, or from the special names of His prophets — meaning: if it were a name that coincides with the name of a prophet from the prophets of Allah the Exalted but the name of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and the Imams (peace be upon them) was not specifically intended, it would not be obligatory to remove it — then he said: [if it specifically names] the Imams (peace be upon them), he must remove it during istinja', he must not bring it into contact with najasah, and he should keep it pure out of veneration for Allah the Exalted and for His awliya' (peace be upon them). This hadith provides evidence for that.

key_terms.الِاسْتِنْجَاءُ: ritual cleansing after answering the call of nature
key_terms.الْمَاءُ الرَّاكِدُ: stagnant/still water — subject to stricter purity rules
key_terms.الْمَاءُ الْجَارِي: flowing/running water — a category in Islamic ritual-purity law that self-purifies

ai.seo_question: What does Shia hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) say about urinating in flowing versus stagnant water, and what are the rules for wearing a ring with divine names during istinja'?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) rules that urinating in flowing water is permissible while urinating in stagnant water is disliked (makruh). Al-Sheikh al-Mufid appends two further rulings from al-Muqni'a: facing or turning one's back to the qibla during answering the call of nature is only disliked in open areas where avoidance is possible, and a ring bearing the names of Allah, the Prophet (SAWW), or the Imams (AS) must be removed during istinja' out of veneration for the sacred names.
